extracted.intended_audience: Authors preparing to submit manuscripts to the American Journal of Political Science (AJPS)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for submitting original and revised manuscripts to the American Journal of Political Science via the Editorial Manager system, including anonymization, human-subjects documentation, supporting information, reviewer exclusions, and required metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript intended for review by AJPS must be submitted through the online editorial system, Editorial Manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions sent by other means will not follow the standard review workflow; use the provided 'Click Here to Submit your Manuscript' link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding author designation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manuscript has multiple authors, then one author must be designated as the corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corresponding author will act for the full team of authors as the sole contact for communications with the AJPS Editorial Offices throughout the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission information authors must have available
rubrics_metrics.description: Before starting the submission process, the corresponding author should have available the names and e-mail addresses of all authors; for each author, the names of those on their dissertation committee and a list of co-authors from the previous five years; the abstract text; and a list of opposed reviewers for the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is required to complete online submission fields and to assist editors in reviewer selection/conflict screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure with editorial team
rubrics_metrics.description: We expect the corresponding author to confirm whether any of the authors on the submitted paper have a conflict of interest with the editorial team, and the nature of that conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear details of the conflict so editors can manage assignment and review appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research subfield and keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: During the submission process, the corresponding author needs to identify a research subfield for the manuscript and designate several keywords that identify the topics for which the manuscript is relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the single best research subfield and multiple keywords so editors and reviewers can properly evaluate topical fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised submission identification
rubrics_metrics.description: An author invited to submit a revised manuscript needs to provide the original manuscript number (i.e., that used during the initial review by the AJPS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the original AJPS manuscript number in the submission metadata to link the revision to prior review files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects and IRB documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose work involves human subjects must provide information regarding how the research was conducted. If any author on a manuscript has access to an institutional IRB, then the research on which the submission is based must have received IRB approval or exemption; the corresponding author will submit documentation of IRB approval or exemption along with the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no author has access to an institutional IRB, the manuscript must include an appendix that addresses a series of questions about the conduct of the research (link provided). If the research relies on publicly available data that received IRB approval for the original data collection, IRB approval or exemption is not required for submission to the AJPS (though this policy may differ from authors’ home institutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous manuscript file requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An original or revised manuscript must include one anonymous (PDF, Word, or LaTex) file. For original submissions, the corresponding author must submit a fully anonymous version of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The file containing the manuscript should be marked 'anonymous' in the document summary tab and the file must be printable. For (invited) revised submissions, the corresponding author must also upload the response memorandum as an anonymous PDF attached to the top of the anonymous manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author Comments / Acknowledgments handling during review
rubrics_metrics.description: A corresponding author may, but is not required to, include comments to the Editor, acknowledgments, and details on where the paper has been presented in the 'Author Comments' field in Editorial Manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the only place that these details should be included while the manuscript is under review; if accepted, they can be added into the final version of the paper submitted for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Information (SI) upload policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If Supporting Information (SI) of no more than 20 pages is included as part of a manuscript submission, it must be uploaded as an 'Appendix' in the Editorial Manager system, and complete the 'Description' text box associated with the SI file with 'Online Appendix.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This designation allows the file to be available to reviewers, but excluded from the print edition of the AJPS if the manuscript is accepted for publication. Note that any file uploaded to Editorial Manager under the 'other' designation will not be accessible to referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposed reviewers disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may also designate up to three people they oppose as reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases, the author must specify why the individual should be disqualified from serving as a referee. The selection of individuals opposed by the authors as reviewers is at the co-editors’ discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance formatting and replication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manuscript is accepted for publication, additional formatting and replication requirements must be met prior to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult 'Guidelines for Accepted Articles' for specific post-acceptance requirements (e.g., replication materials, formatting).
